memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'From the day after the Sabbath, the day you brought the sheaf of the
wave offering, count off seven full weeks. Count off fifty days up to
the day after the seventh Sabbath, and then present an offering of new
grain to the LORD'" - Lev 23:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Fifty days of counting. From the wave sheaf to this new offering,
Israel marked off the weeks one by one. The Greek name for this
festival is Pentecost, meaning fiftieth.

There is something valuable in counting. It builds anticipation. It
keeps a coming event in view during ordinary days. Israel did not
simply stumble into the festival; they walked toward it deliberately.

Dear reader, watch what happened at one particular Pentecost. Jesus had
risen - the firstfruits waved before the Father. Then He told His
disciples to wait in Jerusalem for the gift the Father had promised
(Acts 1:4). They waited. And when the day of Pentecost came, the Spirit
was poured out and about three thousand people were added in a single
day (Acts 2:1-4, 41).

A festival about a new grain harvest became the day of the greatest
spiritual harvest the world had yet seen. God's timing is never
accidental.

Are you in a season of waiting and counting? The disciples spent those
days praying together, not knowing exactly what was coming. Keep
waiting well. God is often preparing something in the counting.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do I handle seasons of waiting on God?
2. Am I waiting passively or actively, in prayer and expectation?
3. What has God promised that I need to keep in view?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, teach me to wait on You well - prayerfully, expectantly, and
without giving up. Thank You that Your timing is always purposeful.
Amen.
